rationale: The LITERAL-CALLEE fabrication, found by the M59.A7 (#825) depth draw and not by reading the analyzer: the 900-file powershell draw (bun script/m14/differential.ts --repo powershell --sample 900) reported exactly one unexplained edge — `calls StartSSHProcess -> false` at src/System.Management.Automation/engine/remoting/common/RunspaceConnectionInfo.cs:2331, a line that assigns a boolean literal. Cause, measured with script/m14/tmp/cs-u2331-probe.ts and reproduced minimally with script/m14/tmp/cs-literal-callee-hunt.ts: after ONE missing semicolon (`… = false` then `return …(...)`), the grammar's error recovery parses the literal and the far-away argument list as ONE invocation_expression, so the node carrying the callee is a `boolean_literal`. The target hygiene at the time checked the target STRING (a keyword set, an identifier-shape check, a builtin set) and `false` is a well-formed identifier to a string check. The rule is now structural: a call's callee must be a NAMING node (identifier or generic_name). The fixture is an ERROR fixture on purpose — the shape cannot exist in a well-formed file — and it carries a LEGAL CONTROL (the same code WITH the semicolon) whose calls must still be emitted, so the fix cannot degenerate into `drop calls near error nodes`. Measured here: Damaged emits no call to the literal, and Legal still emits `calls Legal -> StartSSHProcessImpl` (line 44) and `calls Legal -> GetDirectoryName` (line 41).

expectRelationships.comment: the control: a real call next to the damaged one is still emitted (no blanket suppression)
the damaged method is not silenced wholesale either — only the junk callee is refused
